items.title: Ray Lopez Interview, 1958-08-30
items.q: I go up, I'm walking down Clark Street one day and who I run up at Charlie Mack... He said, you tell Smiley. Make the reservation for the whole show tonight... sure enough, so they went out and bought some flowers and put them all over the table. And up until 11 o'clock, there wasn't a human in the

ctx.x: It burned down 1919, many years ago.

Oh. So, but then, no, it just happened to be in me. I'll tell you. I'll tell you. It was a, when I was working for the Western Union, I joined the Woodmen of the World. The kids, you know. Woodcraft, that's what it was. And then, I said, we need a bugle. So, a policeman out there by the name of Ben McKee. He said, well, I'll get you a bugle if you can play one. I said, well, I'll try it. So, he got me a bugle. And then, I practiced up on it and got a few bugle calls. And that was it. I could play the calls. And…
You were that bad? Freddie didn't want to tell me I was bad. Yeah.
